summary: Discovery focused on security posture for evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Key topics: SOC2/ISO attestations, SSO/SAML and SCIM, RBAC, audit logs and retention, encryption and KMS options, data residency and retention. Radium leans toward Redwood Dedicated or Private for PHI-sensitive workloads but wants to validate attestation and network controls. Next: send docs, schedule deep-dive, Radium to share retention matrix.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for PHI
transcript:
[00:00] Adele (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros — I'm Adele, AE on the Redwood side, with Samir our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Samir (Redwood SE): Hi all, Samir here. I'll jump into the technical bits when you're ready.
[00:20] Lena (Radium VP Eng): Thanks, Adele. I'm Lena, VP Eng at Radium. Mark, Priya and Evan are with me. We're evaluating options for hosting our LLM-based clinical summarization — mostly concerned about PHI handling.
[00:35] Mark (Radium Sec Arch): Yeah, primary questions — what attestations do you have (SOC 2, ISO), how does SSO/SAML integrate, RBAC and what audit logs look like, plus encryption and key management. Also retention — we have strict 7-year audit needs for some datasets.
[00:50] Adele: Totally — that's exactly what we wanted to cover. To set context: Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. For PHI we typically see customers choose Dedicated or Private depending on isolation + contracts.
[01:08] Evan (CTO): Can you summarize the difference from a security control perspective?
[01:12] Samir: Sure — Hosted is our multi-tenant hosted offering with encryption at rest and in transit, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 in our compliance pack, and contractual DPA commitments. Dedicated provides tenant-isolated GPU pools in our cloud, dedicated network peering options, and more stringent isolation controls. Private is an on-prem or VPC deployment where the control plane can be customer-managed.
[01:34] Priya (IT Ops): You mentioned SOC2 and ISO — do you have the certs we can share with our audit team?
[01:39] Adele: Yes, we can share SOC 2 and ISO artifacts — I'll send those after the call (Adele: action). We also keep a security pack with pen test summaries, network diagrams, and our data flow.
[01:50] Mark: For encryption — do you support BYOK via KMS/HSM? We need customer-managed keys for some workflows.
[01:56] Samir: We do. For Dedicated and Private you can bring your own KMS keys — we integrate with major cloud KMS providers, and for Private we can integrate with customer HSMs. For Hosted we support KMS options for workspace-level keys; there are some constraints on full BYOK for multi-tenant hosted, but we can map specifics.
[02:16] Lena: What about audit logs and retention? Our legal requires immutable logs for change events and access for at least 7 years for certain data types.
[02:24] Samir: Logs are retained per plan — Hosted standard retention is 90 days for standard logs but we do offer extended log retention as an add-on. For Dedicated/Private you control the retention window and can ship logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) — we support streaming audit logs and have field-level event types for token usage, model calls, config changes.
[02:45] Mark: Can we get the raw audit schema? We need to confirm immutability and tamper-evidence.
[02:50] Samir: Yes — we'll share the audit schema and the recommended SIEM pipeline. For immutability we typically recommend storing logs in append-only buckets with object lock or in a customer-controlled SIEM with retention policies.
[03:04] Evan: On SSO — we use Okta. How does Redwood support SAML and SCIM for provisioning?
[03:10] Adele: We support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. You can map groups to RBAC roles. We also support enterprise SSO session timeouts and session revocation.
[03:22] Priya: Is there a built-in RBAC model? We need least-privilege roles and auditability for token issuance.
[03:28] Samir: Yes — role-based access control with built-in roles (Admin, Developer, Viewer) and granular route-model policies. Tokens are auditable — we log token creation, scope, and actions. You can also integrate with your identity provider for team mapping via SCIM.
[03:43] Lena: What about data residency? Some of our data must remain in-region (EU/US).
[03:48] Samir: We offer region pinning for workloads on Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be regionally served in certain cloud regions; for strict in-region data residency we typically recommend Dedicated or Private.
[04:02] Mark: One concern — inference caching and KV cache. Does that persist customer data anywhere that could be shared across tenants?
[04:10] Samir: KV cache is per-tenant for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, caching is per-tenant workspace but yes we need to be explicit — we don't share KV caches across customers. We'll provide documentation that spells out lifecycle and eviction policies.
[04:27] Lena: How do you handle data retention for prompt logs and responses? We want to be able to retain certain records for audits but purge PII per retention schedules.
[04:36] Samir: We support configurable retention policies per data type — request logs, generated content, user prompts. For Hosted default is shorter retention, but Dedicated/Private you can set policies and we can implement automated purge jobs. We also support redaction pipelines if you want to strip PII before storage.
[04:55] Priya: Are you PCI/PHI certified or do you have BAAs?
[05:00] Adele: We don't certify as a HIPAA-covered entity, but we sign BAAs for customers handling PHI under certain Dedicated/Private contracts. We also provide SOC2 controls mapping for HIPAA security rule. I'll attach our BAA template for review.
[05:14] Mark: For network topology — can Dedicated be deployed inside our VPC or do you provide peering? We prefer private connectivity.
[05:21] Samir: We provide VPC peering and private connectivity options for Dedicated; Private can be deployed fully inside your VPC or on-prem. We'll share example network diagrams.
[05:32] Evan: Latency — with Dedicated we're expecting predictable latency for streaming inference. Do you have SLOs/SLAs?
[05:38] Adele: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets depending on reserved capacity plan. We'll include the SLA terms in the pricing pack we'll send.
[05:46] Mark: Anything in the pipeline around cert rotations, KMS key rotation, and HSM support for compliance auditors?
[05:53] Samir: Key rotation is supported — you can rotate keys in KMS and we support key versioning; for HSM we can do customer-managed rotation policies. We'll share the key rotation docs and where key access is logged.
[06:08] Lena: Who owns the logs of model outputs? If we use Hosted and want to exclude storage of prompts/outputs, is that possible?
[06:16] Samir: You can opt out of storing prompts/outputs for hosted in certain configurations, but that limits caching and some observability features. For guaranteed non-storage we recommend Dedicated/Private where you control retention and storage.
[06:32] Priya: Do you do periodic third-party pen tests and vulnerability scans?
[06:37] Adele: Yes — we have regular third-party pen tests and internal scans; we can share a summary and remediation cadence.
[06:44] Mark: On logging detail — do logs include token-level cost breakdowns? That's useful for our finance team.
[06:50] Samir: Yes — our Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and the logs include token counts per request so you can map costs.
[07:02] Evan: For a pilot, what's the recommended approach? Hosted with strict logs off? Or Dedicated trial?
[07:09] Adele: For initial eval we often recommend Hosted for speed, but if PHI is in scope, a short Dedicated pilot is common — we can provision a small reserved pool for benchmarking and run against your sample prompts.
[07:23] Mark: We're concerned about SIEM integration. Which log formats do you support?
[07:27] Samir: We export JSON event streams, syslog, and have native integrations with Splunk and Datadog. We'll share a sample event stream.
[07:38] Priya: Any limitations on SCIM provisioning — does it support nested groups?
[07:42] Samir: SCIM support is standard; nested groups vary by IdP but we can map a workaround using group-mapping rules. We'll capture specifics in the tech deep-dive.
[07:55] Lena: Can you show us the role matrix? We need to map our internal roles to Redwood roles.
[08:00] Adele: We'll attach the RBAC matrix with the follow-up.
[08:04] Mark: One red flag we've seen with other vendors is noisy metadata leakage via logs or telemetry. How do you ensure PII or PHI isn't accidentally sent to analytics buckets?
[08:15] Samir: We scrub PII by default in telemetry and we have a telemetry filtering pipeline. For Dedicated/Private you can also disable telemetry exports. We'll provide specifics and examples.
[08:29] Evan: What about data deletion requests for compliance?
[08:33] Adele: We have procedures to handle data deletion requests; for Hosted we have a documented process and for Dedicated/Private you retain control and can enforce deletion policies.
[08:44] Priya: Can we get a list of sub-processors and their locations?
[08:48] Adele: Yes — we'll send the sub-processor list and cloud region map.
[08:52] Mark: Are you encrypting in transit with TLS everywhere?
[08:56] Samir: Yes — TLS 1.2+ in transit and AES-256 at rest for stored data.
[09:03] Lena: Any limitations on model snapshots being stored? Our audits want to ensure models aren't exfiltrated.
[09:09] Samir: Model artifacts are managed; in Dedicated/Private you can pin model versions and control snapshot exports. We'll include the model artifact handling doc.
[09:22] Adele: Quick recap — we'll send SOC2/ISO and BAA template, audit schema, RBAC matrix, network diagrams, KMS/HSM and key rotation docs, log schema and SIEM examples, and Dedicated pricing/SLA. Samir will schedule a tech deep-dive.
[09:36] Priya: Sounds good. Timeline-wise we hope to choose a vendor in June.
[09:40] Evan: We'll get you the retention matrix and compliance checklist by next week.
[09:44] Adele: Great — we'll follow up. Thanks everyone.
[09:47] Mark: Thanks, bye.
[09:49] [call ends]
